events.text: The cranes that carry news between the isles have begun to carry a new name with yours, and you heard it yourself today on the Drifting Market, from two immortals who did not know you were standing behind them.

choices.text: Answer to it

effects.log: You do not correct them.

choices.text: Keep what you are called

effects.log: You lean over and tell them your name, the one you already had.

events.text: An archivist of the Jade Court catches your sleeve after the gathering: the Court's register wants to write a title beside your name, the one the Isles have been using, and only waits for your nod.

choices.text: Nod

effects.log: The archivist writes it in, in a very good hand.

choices.text: Shake your head

effects.log: The archivist puts the brush down, a little disappointed.

events.text: A junior of another order bows to you on the cloud road and calls you by a name you have never answered to, as if everyone knew it already. Perhaps everyone does.

choices.text: Bow back and let the name stand

effects.log: You let it stand. The junior goes away glowing.

choices.text: Tell the junior your own name

effects.log: The junior apologises three times and does not believe you.

events.text: You know this long hall. You remember how it smelled the day your last life ended because of the order that owns it, and here it is again, ordinary and sunny, and nobody in it knows your face yet.

choices.text: Keep your face still and learn them again

effects.log: You learn them again, quietly. They see a newcomer.

choices.text: Strike where you remember they are weak

ok.log: They were weak exactly there. It works.

fail.log: They were not weak there in this life. Now they are watching you.

choices.text: Go in and sit down with them instead

effects.log: You go in. Nobody there has done anything to you yet.

events.text: An elder of the order that cast you down passes you on the cloud road and nods, the way one nods to a stranger. In your last life you watched that elder sign the order that ended it.

choices.text: Nod back

effects.log: You nod back. Your hand does not shake. Much.

choices.text: Follow, and find what they are hiding this time

ok.log: They are hiding the same thing. You know where to look.

fail.log: They are hiding something else this time, and they see you looking.

choices.text: Call after them, and ask them to tea

effects.log: They are surprised. They come. It is a strange tea.

events.text: The order that cast you down is moving the way you remember, toward the day it moved against you. You can see the shape of it from here, years ahead, like weather over the cloud sea.

choices.text: Stay out of its way for now

effects.log: You stay out of its way. The weather goes by.

choices.text: Cut one of the threads before it is tied

ok.log: You cut it. Somewhere in their hall a plan does not quite come together.

fail.log: You reach for the thread and someone else is already holding it.

choices.text: Warn the one who signed it last time

effects.log: You tell them what you are afraid of, without telling them how you know. They listen.

events.text: Someone in the order that cast you down has started asking how a newcomer always seems to know where to stand. It is a good question. You asked it yourself once, about somebody else.

choices.text: Be wrong on purpose, once or twice

effects.log: You are wrong twice, carefully. The question goes quiet.

choices.text: Make sure the question never reaches the elders

fail.log: It reaches them faster for your trying.

choices.text: Answer the question honestly, to one person

effects.log: You tell one person the truth. They do not laugh.

events.text: The day comes, as you knew it would, and this time it is the order that stands in the middle of the Jade Court with nowhere to step, and you who know every thread of what was done.

choices.text: Pull every thread

effects.log: You pull every thread, and the order comes apart in front of the whole Court.

choices.text: Pull just enough

effects.log: You pull just enough. It is humbled, and it will remember who did it.

events.text: The day comes, as you knew it would, and nothing happens. The elder who signed the order last time is sitting across from you over cloud-tea instead, talking about the weather above the Ninth Isle.

choices.text: Talk about the weather

effects.log: You talk about the weather until the tea is cold. It is the best conversation of two lives.

choices.text: Tell them, at last, what happened the other time

effects.log: You tell them. They are quiet a long while. Then they pour more tea.

events.text: They know. Not how, not what you are, but enough: the elders of the order that cast you down are waiting for you in their long hall, and the doors behind you have been shut.

choices.text: Go over the wall before they ask

effects.log: You go over the wall and the clouds take you somewhere else.

choices.text: Stand and answer them

ok.log: You answer them so well that they let you keep your secret, and your seat.

fail.log: Your answer does not satisfy them. You leave by the wall after all.

events.text: Your old house above the clouds has almost nobody left in it: two ancient disciples sweeping a hall too big for them, and a plaque with your old name on it gone green with cloud-moss.

choices.text: Pick up a broom and help them

effects.log: You sweep with them all day. By evening they are calling you by a name that was yours once.

choices.text: Leave it to the wind

effects.log: You leave. The disciples go on sweeping.

events.text: Under the old hall there is a vault the house's founder sealed with a breath only the founder knew. The two old disciples watch you kneel in front of it. They do not know what you are about to try.

choices.text: Breathe the founder's breath

ok.log: The seal knows you. The vault opens on stores and slips the house thought were lost.

fail.log: The seal does not quite know you in this body. You will have to come back.

choices.text: Leave the vault sealed

effects.log: Some things can stay buried. You turn to the debts instead.

events.text: The order that has been taking your old house's isles one by one sends a junior to laugh at the gate. You remember that order's founder. You remember what they were afraid of.

choices.text: Answer the junior on the platform

ok.log: The junior goes home and tells their elders, and the isles stop being taken.

fail.log: The junior goes home laughing. You will have to answer them again.

choices.text: Send their founder a message only you could write

effects.log: The isles stop being taken by the next gathering. Nobody in that order knows why.

events.text: Your old house stands again. There are disciples in its hall and lanterns on its rail, and somebody has scraped the moss off the plaque. The old name on it is yours, and also it is not.

choices.text: Take the seat at the head of the hall

effects.log: You take it. It fits as if it had been waiting.

choices.text: Give the seat to the oldest disciple, and go on

effects.log: The oldest disciple weeps. You go on, lighter.
